title: phase-gate install receipt
description: Written to .claude/phase-gate-install/receipt.json in the ADOPTER's repo after a real --apply run (the installer skill's step 5). This is the durable record of what actually happened, and - critically - what version of phase-gate produced it. Without source_commit and manifest_version, no future update path can ever tell 'phase-gate changed this since you installed' from 'you edited this yourself' (build spec finding 10, modeled on copier's .copier-answers.yml _commit field and kubectl apply's last-applied-configuration annotation).

installed_at.description: When this apply actually ran, ISO 8601.

source_commit.description: The phase-gate repo's git SHA that was actually installed. Carried through unchanged from the plan that preceded this apply (plan.schema.json's source_commit) - the two MUST match; a mismatch means the adopter approved one plan and a different commit got applied, which is itself a bug worth surfacing loudly.

source_origin.description: The git remote URL the adopter confirmed at step 0 (whatever remote name it was - origin, upstream, or otherwise; never assumed), with any embedded userinfo (user:token@) stripped before being recorded here. Required, not optional: an old receipt predating this field already lacks it regardless of required-ness, but making it optional would let a future install silently omit it - the same silent-degradation shape this project rejects elsewhere (see source_commit/manifest_version's own required-ness). Lets a later update-check compare against the adopter's own actual remote (their fork included) instead of a hardcoded canonical URL.

manifest_version.description: The installer/manifest.json schema_version this install was built against.

adopter_repo_root.description: Absolute path to the adopter's repo root this was installed into.

variables.description: The FINAL resolved value of every variable actually used during this install - same shape as the plan's variables array, but these are facts about what happened, not a forecast.

source.description: See plan.schema.json's matching field - 'confirmed_none' is a deliberate, informed 'this genuinely does not apply' answer, distinct from 'left_empty' (unaddressed).

components.description: Every component ever installed across this receipt's history, merge-forward (build spec finding F2, 2026-09-06): each write starts from the prior receipt's own entries (if one exists), overwrites only the files this run actually wrote, and carries every other prior entry through unchanged. An entry's own written_this_run flag (see files_written below) is what distinguishes the two - the array itself is never replaced wholesale, only ever merged into.

files_written.description: Every file this component has ever had written in the adopter's repo (merged forward across every install/upgrade run - see the array's own description above), each with a content hash so a later re-run (step 6) can tell 'unchanged since install' from 'locally modified' without trusting a stale claim.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the file's content with all line endings normalized to LF first (CRLF/CR -> LF) - the export enforces LF via .gitattributes, but the adopter's own checkout, editor, or OS may not, and a line-ending-only diff must never register as a real modification.

written_this_run.description: true only if this specific apply run actually wrote this file (content_hash is fresh); false means this entry was carried forward unchanged from a prior receipt. verify_citations.py's check 1 (citation re-verification) uses this to skip re-checking only the entries actually written this run - carried-forward entries stay fully re-checked, same as anything never installed. Check 1b (receipt file hashes) re-validates every entry regardless of this flag, written_this_run or not - that is the mechanism that actually closes F2 (an upgrade touching 3 of 45 files no longer silently drops hash protection for the other 42).

repo_files.description: Every installer/manifest.json repo_files entry ever installed across this receipt's history, same merge-forward contract as components above - docs/methodology.md above all, since it is the one repo_files entry every skill's own text depends on.

path.description: Relative to adopter_repo_root - the plan's own repo_files[].path (which is the manifest entry's target_path when one exists, e.g. installer/phase-gate-install/SKILL.md lands at .claude/skills/phase-gate-install/SKILL.md - otherwise identical to the manifest entry's own path).

content_hash.description: sha256 of the file's content, LF-normalized - same contract as components' files_written.content_hash.

written_this_run.description: Same contract as components' files_written.written_this_run - true only if this run actually wrote this file, false if carried forward unchanged from a prior receipt.

settings_merge.description: The result of the merge_settings.py step, if any settings.json changes were part of this install.

fragments_merged.description: Which settings.fragment.json / settings.hooks.json files were merged in.

hook_entries_written.description: Every (event, matcher, type, command) hook tuple this export's fragments have ever added to settings.json across this receipt's whole history, merge-forward the same contract as components[].files_written above - each entry's own written_this_run distinguishes what this specific run added from what a prior run already established. Populated only from merge_settings.py's own --report-json output (installer/merge_settings.py's compute_hook_report) - never hand-transcribed from its text diff, since only the script itself can correctly tell an appended tuple from one already present. Required for phase-gate-uninstall to safely reverse a merge without needing the original phase-gate clone; see hook_entries_complete below for what an old-shaped receipt lacking this field means.

matcher.description: The matcher-group's own matcher field, or null if the event doesn't use one.

written_this_run.description: Same merge-forward contract as components[].files_written.written_this_run - true only if this specific run's merge_settings.py call actually appended this tuple; false means carried forward unchanged from a prior receipt.

status_line_written.description: The exact statusLine object value this export's own fragment set, present only if merge_settings.py's --report-json reported it with no conflict (absent/null if no fragment in this install ever set statusLine, or if every attempt hit a pre-existing different value). Overwritten wholesale on each run that sets it - unlike hook_entries_written, there is only ever one statusLine value to track, not a merge-forward list.

hook_entries_complete.description: False whenever this run's receipt write starts from a prior receipt that itself lacks hook_entries_written (an upgrade from a receipt predating this field) - true on a fresh install, or an upgrade from a receipt that already had it. Checking hook_entries_written's mere presence is not enough to know it covers the receipt's ENTIRE history rather than only recent runs; phase-gate-uninstall must check this flag, not just field presence, before trusting hook_entries_written/status_line_written as a complete record.

verification.description: Optional: results of verify_citations.py and/or the class-1/2/3/4 risk-class checks the installer skill ran, if it recorded them here rather than only printing them.
